newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Fire in south Philippines hotel kills 23.
newsitem.headline: Fire in south Philippines hotel kills 23.

text.p: Twenty-three people died and 20 others were injured when a fire raged through a six-storey hotel in the southern Philippines early on Saturday, forcing guests to jump for their lives out of windows.
Some broke their legs as they leapt to escape the deadliest fire in the country since 152 revelers, mostly teenagers, were killed in a Manila disco fire in March last year.
Foreign diplomats had been booked to stay at the popular Imperial Hotel in Cotabato for a Moslem celebration from Sunday.
Police initially reported eight people were killed but police inspector Jaime Guadilla said firemen recovered 15 more bodies in the upper floors after battling their way through heavy smoke.
"We saw other bodies in the burned rooms," Guadilla said.
The fire, which gutted three floors of the building, broke out in a prayer room used by both Moslems and Christians. Only a few dozen guests were in when the blaze started at 12.30 a.m.
It was unclear what caused the inferno, fire investigators said.

Local officials said the hotel had been getting ready for the arrival on Sunday of foreign diplomats and Philippine dignitaries attending a state-of-the-region address by former Moslem rebel chief Nur Misuari, who now runs a four-province Moslem autonomous region on the southern island of Mindanao.

Misuari, who signed a peace agreeement with Manila last year ending a 24-year Moslem revolt for autonomy, has his headquarters in Cotabato, a predominantly Moslem city 900 km (560 miles) south of Manila.
Witnesses said guests leapt through their windows, some wearing only their underwear, in order to escape the blaze.
"I jumped like Superman. Now, you see my legs are broken," local Moslem official Nur Baiman told Reuters while undergoing treatment at a local hospital.

Saudi Arabian preacher Al Daruis, who suffered bruises, said he escaped by wrapping himself up with a water-soaked blanket and running down a burning hallway on the third floor of the hotel in the city centre.
"I was fortunate because I was awake...I was praying," Daruis said. "I smelt smoke and when I opened the door the hallway was full of smoke...I called downstairs and people said there was a fire."
He then grabbed his blanket and drenched it in water.
"I was asleep in my room when I woke up feeling as if I was choking. It was the smoke," said Jimmy Malcampo, who survived with leg injuries after leaping through a third floor window.
"I rushed out of my room and saw the hall on fire. My choice was to die or jump out of the window. I jumped," he said.
Roger Araila said he was wearing only his briefs when he jumped through the window of his third floor room, also breaking his legs.
Some survived by climbing down firemen's ladders.
Chief arson investigator Abdulazak Mosa said some of the victims suffocated after being trapped in their rooms or in hallways while trying to flee from the two-and-a-half hour fire.
"We have not determined whether the fire was accidental or intentional. We are still investigating," he said.
A hotel official said: "It could have been worse if the fire happened later because we were expecting foreign dignitaries."
